19569-the-guests-of-hercules.title: Guests of Hercules
19569-the-guests-of-hercules.creator: C. N. and A. M. WILLIAMSON
19569-the-guests-of-hercules.description: A book by C. N. and A. M. WILLIAMSON. There was a smell of autumn on the windless air, bitter yet sweet; the scent of dying leaves, and fading flowers loth to perish, of rose-berries that had usurped the place of roses, of chrysanthemums chilled by frost, of moist earth deprived of sun, and of the green moss-like film overgrowing all the trunks of the old beech trees.

arxiv-1507-02520.title: Heavy Mesons Spectroscopy
arxiv-1507-02520.creator: N. Tazimi M. MonemzadehM. R. Hadizadeh
arxiv-1507-02520.description: Abstract In this paper, we use Martin and Coulomb-Linear potentials and solve Lippman-Schwinger equation and then identify b ​ c ¯ b\bar{c} energy levels. Moreover, we predict results for such energy levels as that of t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} (in its short half-life) which is not observed. We showed our results are consistent with previous findings in literature.

arxiv-2302-03738.title: Vorticity cascade and turbulent drag in wall-bounded flows: plane Poiseuille flow
arxiv-2302-03738.creator: Samvit Kumar 1, Charles Meneveau 1, Gregory Eyink 1,2
arxiv-2302-03738.description: Abstract Drag for wall-bounded flows is directly related to the spatial flux of spanwise vorticity outward from the wall. In turbulent flows a key contribution to this wall-normal flux arises from nonlinear advection and stretching of vorticity, interpretable as a cascade.

arxiv-2307-12508.title: Information Geometry of Wasserstein Statistics on Shapes and Affine Deformations
arxiv-2307-12508.creator: Shun-ichi Amari, Takeru Matsuda
arxiv-2307-12508.description: Abstract Information geometry and Wasserstein geometry are two main structures introduced in a manifold of probability distributions, and they capture its different characteristics. We study characteristics of Wasserstein geometry in the framework of [ 34 ] for the affine deformation statistical model, which is a multi-dimensional generalization of the location-scale model.

arxiv-2312-00527.title: An investigation of information flux between turbulent boundary layer and porous medium
arxiv-2312-00527.creator: Xu Chu, Wenkang Wang, Bernhard Weigand
arxiv-2312-00527.description: Abstract The interaction between boundary layer turbulence and a porous layer is the cornerstone to the interface engineering. In this study, the spatial resolved transfer entropy is used to assess the asymmetry of the causal interaction next to a permeable wall. The analysis was based on pore-resolved direct numerical simulation of turbulent channel flow over a cylinder array.

arxiv-2402-03672.title: The spin alignment of rho mesons in a pion gas
arxiv-2402-03672.creator: Yi-Liang Yin, Wen-Bo Dong, Jin-Yi Pang, Shi Pu, Qun Wang
arxiv-2402-03672.description: Abstract We study the spin alignment of neutral rho mesons in a pion gas using spin kinetic or Boltzmann equations. The ρ ​ π ​ π \rho\pi\pi coupling is given by the chiral effective theory. The collision terms at the leading and next-to-leading order in spin Boltzmann equations are derived.

arxiv-2402-04181.title: Longevity Studies of CSC Prototypes Operating with Ar+CO 2 Gas Mixture and Different Fractions of CF 4
arxiv-2402-04181.creator: Emanuela Barberis, Nebojsa Begovic, Nicholas Haubrich, Mikhail Ignatenko, Andrey Korytov, Ota Kukral, Ekaterina Kuznetsova, Armando Lanaro, Andrew MacCabe, Predrag Milenovic, Dubravka Milovanovic, Guenakh Mitselmakher, Aleksandra Radulovic, Boris Rajcic, Jake Rosenzweig, Bingran Wang, Jian Wang, And
arxiv-2402-04181.description: Abstract Studies of Cathode Strip Chamber longevity, comparing Ar+CO 2 gas mixtures with fractions of 5%, 2%, and 0% CF 4 , were performed using several small cathode strip prototype chambers. In each trial, a localized source of radiation was used to irradiate up to an accumulated charge of about 300 mC/cm.

arxiv-2403-03291.title: Dynamical Logical Qubits in the Bacon-Shor Code
arxiv-2403-03291.creator: M. Sohaib Alam, Eleanor Rieffel
arxiv-2403-03291.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by M. Sohaib Alam, Eleanor Rieffel. The Bacon-Shor code is a quantum error correcting subsystem code composed of weight 2 check operators that admits a single logical qubit, and has distance d d on a d × d d\times d square lattice. We show that when viewed as a Floquet code, by choosing an appropriate measurement schedule of the check operators, it can additionally host several dynamical logical qubits.

arxiv-2404-09607.title: Better space-time-robustness trade-offs for set reconciliation
arxiv-2404-09607.creator: Djamal Belazzougui, Gregory Kucherov, Stefan Walzer
arxiv-2404-09607.description: Abstract We consider the problem of reconstructing the symmetric difference between similar sets from their representations (sketches) of size linear in the number of differences. Exact solutions to this problem are based on error-correcting coding techniques and suffer from a large decoding time.

arxiv-2405-03846.title: Enhancing Apparent Personality Trait Analysis with Cross-Modal Embeddings
arxiv-2405-03846.description: Abstract Automatic personality trait assessment is essential for high-quality human-machine interactions. Systems capable of human behavior analysis could be used for self-driving cars, medical research, and surveillance, among many others. We present a multimodal deep neural network with a Siamese extension for apparent personality trait prediction trained on short video recordings and exploiting modality invariant embeddings.

arxiv-2411-12793.title: Deep Boundary Perturbations at a Quantum Critical Point
arxiv-2411-12793.creator: Shang Liu
arxiv-2411-12793.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shang Liu. In this work, we explore an unconventional class of problems in the study of (quantum) critical phenomena, termed “deep boundary criticality”. Traditionally, critical systems are analyzed with two types of perturbations: those uniformly distributed throughout the bulk, which can significantly alter the bulk criticality by triggering a nontrivial bulk renormalization group flow, and those confined to a boundary or subdimensional defect, which affect only the boundary or defect condition.

arxiv-2510-17314.title: Auto-Rubric: Learning to Extract Generalizable Criteria for Reward Modeling
arxiv-2510-17314.creator: Lipeng Xie, Sen Huang, Zhuo Zhang, Anni Zou, Yunpeng Zhai, Dingchao Ren, Kezun Zhang, Haoyuan Hu, Boyin Liu, Haoran Chen, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding
arxiv-2510-17314.description: Abstract Reward models are essential for aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human values, yet their development is hampered by costly preference datasets and poor interpretability. While recent rubric-based approaches offer transparency, they often lack systematic quality control and optimization, creating a trade-off between scalability and reliability.

pmc-10704061.title: Cardiac Surgery Morbidity and Mortality in Hypertensive and Arrhythmic Patients: A Retrospective Analysis
pmc-10704061.creator: Abdullah Abdulrahman Bayazed, Abdullah Khalid Alassiri, Abdullah Alaa Farid, Muhannad Salem Dawood, Khalid Mohammed Alshuqayfi, Abdulaziz Mustafa Adnan, Faisal Othman BinJahlan, Turki Bader Aljohani, Ragab Shehata Debis, Khalid E Al-Ebrahim
pmc-10704061.description: Background: Hypertension (HTN) is the most significant modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD) and overall mortality. HTN is defined as a systolic blood pressure of ≥140 mmHg and/or a diastolic blood pressure of ≥ 90 mmHg. Generally, arrhythmias are characterized by a disruption of the heart's regular rhythm.

pmc-11354270.title: Density Gradient Centrifugation Is an Effective Tool to Isolate Cancer Stem-like Cells from Hypoxic and Normoxia Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Models
pmc-11354270.creator: Camillo Sargiacomo, Aleksandr Klepinin, Christos Papadimitriou
pmc-11354270.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Accumulating evidence has indicated that stemness-related genes are associated with the aggressiveness of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Because no universal markers for breast CSCs are available, we applied the density gradient centrifugation method to enrich breast CSCs. We demonstrated that the density centrifugation method allows for the isolation of cancer stem cells (CSCs) from adherent and non-adherent MCF7 (Luminal A), MDA-MB-231 (TNBC) and MDA-MB-468 (TNBC) breast cancer cells.

pmc-11465257.title: Optimizing Methane Control in Composite Goaf Areas: Insights from Multisource Emission Analysis and Numerical Modeling in the Tongxin Coal Mine
pmc-11465257.creator: Chungang Liu
pmc-11465257.description: Coal mine methane poses a threat to both coal production and the well-being of workers. This study investigates the complex challenge of managing methane emissions from multiple sources in coal mines prone to gas. Coal mining creates multiple air leakage channels in the mine goaf, increasing the risk of gas explosions.

pmc-12386168.title: Unveiling the Dark Side of Negative Behaviors Among Nurses and Their Implications in Workforce Well-Being and Patient Care: A Scoping Review
pmc-12386168.creator: Nuno Santos, Rita Barahona, Paulo Cruchinho, Elisabete Nunes, Alessandro Stievano
pmc-12386168.description: Introduction: Negative behaviors in nursing undermine well-being, erode team cohesion, and jeopardize patient safety. Rooted in systemic stressors—workload, emotional strain, and power imbalances—they have far-reaching effects on job satisfaction and care quality. Objective: To systematically map the scientific evidence on negative behaviors among nurses in healthcare organizations.

pmc-12641984.title: Everyday Auditory Environment Among Elderly Cochlear Implant Users
pmc-12641984.creator: Ulrika Larsson, Ulrika Löfkvist, Karin Hallin, Andrea Ciorba, Daniele Borsetto
pmc-12641984.description: Background/Objectives: For most adults receiving a cochlear implant (CI), the primary goal is to enhance their oral communication with others. The aim of this study was to investigate the total CI usage time per day among retired CI users and to characterize in which auditory environments they were using their CI.

pmc-12644495.title: Machine-learning and simulation identify food-derived xanthine oxidase inhibitors with in-vitro activity
pmc-12644495.creator: Bo Yu, Zhen Qin, Yuxi Wu, Chengsong He
pmc-12644495.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Gout is a common metabolic disorder caused by hyperuricaemia, with xanthine oxidase (XO) playing a key role in uric acid production. Food-derived XO inhibitors are therefore of interest as candidate chemotypes, although any nutraceutical application will require in-vivo validation. In this study, we developed an integrated in-silico workflow that combines machine learning, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) to prioritize potential inhibitors.

From day 1, experimental groups were dietary supplemented with C.

pmc-13187335.title: Meta-learned dynamic hierarchical fusion for robust multi-scale object classification
pmc-13187335.creator: Prashanta Kumar Patra, Amitav Mahapatra
pmc-13187335.description: A key limitation of existing feature fusion methods is their static nature: they learn dataset-specific integration policies during training that remain fixed at inference. This restricts adaptability to new domains and input characteristics, often causing brittle generalization, hierarchical information decay, and inefficient relational modeling. We propose Meta-Learned Dynamic Hierarchical Fusion (MDHF), which reframes feature fusion as context-conditioned policy generation.

pmc-13197154.title: Innovation Deimplementation in Emergency Departments During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Qualitative Study of Clinicians’ Decision-Making
pmc-13197154.creator: Shreya Huilgol, Nabeel Qureshi, Carl Berdahl, Catherine Cohen, Peter Mendel, Shira Fischer, Matthew Balcarras
pmc-13197154.description: BackgroundDuring a public health emergency, emergency department (ED) clinicians can improve care delivery if they identify and adopt innovations that are safe and effective. However, little is known about the factors that impact ED clinicians’ decision-making around using or discontinuing innovations when evidence-based information is limited.

pmc-13402667.title: The relationship between medical workers’ presence of meaning in life and turnover intention: the mediating role of searching for meaning in life and professional happiness
pmc-13402667.creator: Zihan Zheng, Huilin Zhang, Yuting Huang, Siyu Su, Zuming Qin, Jiao Cheng, Zhiling Feng
pmc-13402667.description: The high turnover rate of medical workers has become a global problem. This study aims to explore the relationship between the presence of meaning in life and turnover intention among medical workers, and to examine the mediating role of the search for meaning in life and professional happiness. The study conducted a cross-sectional survey involving 1125 Chinese medical workers.

pmc-13589272.title: Medicaid Expansion and Mortality Among Patients With Colorectal Cancer
pmc-13589272.creator: Oluwasegun Akinyemi, Oladayo Oyebanji, Babawale Oluborode, Bolarinwa Akinwumi, Fadeke Ogunyankin, Kakra Hughes, Terrence Fullum, Quyen Chu, Surya Nalamati, Marwan Abouljoud, Christine Nembhard, Craig Reickert
pmc-13589272.description: Key PointsQuestionWhat is the association of Medicaid expansion with overall survival in colorectal cancer, as well as with stage at diagnosis, treatment patterns, and survival benefits across racial and ethnic groups and disease stages?FindingsIn this cohort study of 658 593 adults with colorectal cancer, Medicaid expansion was associated with a 6.3% relative reduction in overall mortality hazard.
